source.located: The five literals are the CODATA 2018 recommended values (Tiesinga, Mohr, Newell, Taylor, RMP 93, 025010 (2021); no arXiv copy) and, for m_e and m_p, the PDG RPP 2024/2025 values, which are the CODATA 2018 numbers. Superseded by CODATA 2022 (Mohr, Newell, Taylor, Tiesinga, arXiv:2409.03787, RMP 97, 025002 (2025)) and, for m_e/m_p, by PDG RPP 2026.

published_statement: CODATA 2018 (as READ in the NIST table and restated verbatim by PDG 2024): m_e c^2 = 0.510 998 950 00(15) MeV; m_p c^2 = 938.272 088 16(29) MeV; proton rms charge radius r_p = 0.8414(19) x 10^-15 m; Bohr radius a_0 = 5.291 772 109 03(80) x 10^-11 m; alpha^-1 = 137.035 999 084(21), 'CODATA recommended value at Q^2 = 0' (PDG 2024 footnote). CODATA 2022 (READ, arXiv:2409.03787): 0.510 998 950 69(16) MeV; 938.272 089 43(29) MeV; r_p = 8.4075(64) x 10^-16 m; a_0 = 5.291 772 105 44(82) x 10^-11 m; alpha^-1 = 137.035 999 177(21).
published_hypotheses: A least-squares adjustment over all input data judged relevant and consistent, with expansion factors applied where inputs disagree (2.5 on the six alpha-determining items D1-D6 in 2022, p.62) -- the adjustment's internal method is READ only in summary here.

r_p (2018) combined H/D spectroscopy, muonic hydrogen Lamb shift and e-p scattering; r_p (2022) EXCLUDES scattering 'because there is a lack of consensus on how the experimental data should be analyzed' (p.2, READ).
r_p is defined as the rms charge radius entering the leading finite-size term eq.(50), which is model-independent at order (Z alpha)^4 and carries the reduced-mass factor (m_r/m_e)^3 (p.15, READ).
alpha is the low-energy (Q^2 = 0) value, determined from atom-recoil (Cs, Rb) and a_e measurements (p.62 READ; PDG 2024 footnote READ).
Values are for the physical world (present vacuum), not functions of the Higgs vev: no CODATA statement concerns how r_p, m_e or alpha vary with v.
hypothesis_drift: LABEL/VINTAGE (address.py:424-429): the tree's comment says 'PDG/CODATA' without a year; the values are CODATA 2018 = PDG 2024/2025 exactly (READ), and are NOT the current CODATA 2022 / PDG 2026 values. A dropped qualifier (vintage), not a wrong value.

ADDED, and named by the tree (address.py:47-49, 847-848 'alpha fixed and r_N fixed (H2), so x = r_N/a_0 is proportional to m_e, hence to v'): holding r_p fixed as v varies is the tree's H2, outside anything CODATA measures; CODATA gives r_p at the physical v only. Not a drift from the source; recorded so it is not mistaken for a CODATA statement.

DROPPED FACTOR (address.py:844-862, finite_size_K_sympy; closed form at 834-841): CODATA 2022 eq.(50), READ p.15, carries (m_r/m_e)^3 in the leading finite-size term; the tree's shift '(4/3) Z^4 x^2/n^3 Rydberg' sets m_r = m_e. Computed (sympy): with the factor K = 28 rho^2 x^2/(14 rho^2 x^2 - 9), rho = m_r/m_e = 0.999455679, so |K| is SMALLER by 0.1088% -- 11x the W10 pin tolerance (1e-4, address.py:1610-1611), no verdict affected. The tree names 'recoil (m_e/M) omitted, which only adds' (address.py:849); for this particular recoil factor the direction is a decrease -- a discrepancy in the phrase, recorded, not a refutation (the full recoil contribution to the ratio is not computed here).

STRENGTHENED, harmless (address.py:848 'uniform-sphere nucleus, leading order'): eq.(50) needs only the rms radius, not a uniform-sphere model; the tree's model hypothesis is stronger than required and gives the same leading term.

PRECISION (address.py:1610-1611): K_FINITE_SIZE_HYDROGEN is pinned at -7.8654e-10 to 1e-4, but CODATA 2018's own u_r(r_p) = 2.26e-3 gives K a u_r of 4.5e-3 -- the pin is 45x tighter than the datum supports. The same holds for 'lambda_h in proton radii' 1.8732e-3 @1e-3 (address.py:1397), which already sits at +5.49e-4 on 2018 data through the m_h switch 125.20 -> 125.13. Over-precision of a pin, not an error in any conclusion.

alpha AT LOW ENERGY (address.py:570, the tree's stated hypothesis 'alpha at low energy used in K_alpha'): consistent with the source -- CODATA alpha is the Q^2 = 0 value (PDG 2024 footnote, READ), and d ln alpha(0)/d ln m = -alpha(0) d(alpha^-1(0))/d ln m exactly (sympy identity), so alpha(0) is the correct input to 43 alpha/(54 pi) at one loop. No drift.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis has a real instance here, and the evidence cuts both ways. FOR: the proton radius is exactly a case where earlier adjustments lacked data -- CODATA 2006/2010/2014 put r_p at 0.8768-0.8775 fm from H spectroscopy and e-p scattering; the muonic-hydrogen Lamb shift and newer H measurements moved it to 0.8414 fm in 2018, a -3.85% shift of 5.27 combined sigma (computed from the READ tables), and CODATA 2022 then dropped scattering altogether because its analysis lacks consensus (READ). alpha likewise moved 4.5 u(2018) when LKB-20 arrived, and its three inputs still disagree at 5.5 sigma (Cs vs Rb). AGAINST, for this tree: none of it changes a conclusion. W10's K scales as r_p^2, so a pre-2018 radius would make |K| 8-9% larger and a PRad-like radius 2.5% smaller -- the claim 'optical/optical is NOT exactly blind' needs only K != 0, which holds at every radius (a point nucleus is the only way to get zero). Every other rests_on_it number moves by <= 2.7e-9. What the tree carries is the CODATA 2018 vintage, superseded but not wrong; the only consequence of the newer data is that two tight numeric pins (W10 K @1e-4 and lambda_h/r_p @1e-3) fail with CODATA 2022 inputs, which is an over-precision of pins (K's own 2018 u_r is 4.5e-3), not a moved verdict.
grade_evidence: The five literals are the CODATA 2018 values digit for digit (READ in the NIST table and in PDG 2024's verbatim restatement; m_e and m_p also = PDG 2024/2025 mass tables). Each table is internally consistent to <1e-11. CODATA 2022 (READ) supersedes them: m_e, m_p, a_0, alpha by 4.4-4.6 u(2018) (~1e-9 relative), r_p by -0.34 u(2018) (-7.7e-4). Recomputed, no rests_on_it conclusion moves: K_finite stays negative and nonzero across the whole historical and contested r_p span (factor 1.119), K_alpha(H1), the probe ceiling, eps >= 1.80e-5, a_0/lambda_h and S_SCAN[0] move <= 2.7e-9. Sandbox selftests with 2022 values and with 2014/scattering radii: 0 verdict flips; two numeric pins fail, both through r_p. Recorded, not repaired: the tree's 'PDG/CODATA' label omits the vintage; its finite-size shift omits eq.(50)'s (m_r/m_e)^3 (|K| -0.109%, beyond the 1e-4 pin, not the verdict); the W10 pin is 45x tighter than r_p's own uncertainty. The status word NAMED-NOT-READ in address.py is now READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT for 2018 and READ for 2022. Not STANDS-by-default: the later-literature search could not run (quota), so 'no post-2022 datum moves it' is established only up to CODATA 2022 / PDG 2026.
what_would_change_the_grade: DATA-DEPENDENT only if a tree conclusion came to hinge on r_p at the ~1% level (none does now: the verdict needs K != 0) or on m_e/a_0/alpha at <1e-8. NARROWED if the tree's printed K (-7.8654e-10 at 5 s.f.) were treated as a physical result rather than a CODATA-2018-conditional number, since the omitted (m_r/m_e)^3 factor (-0.109%), recoil terms the tree itself names, and r_p's own uncertainty (4.5e-3 in K) all exceed its pin. WRONG only if a literal were shown to differ from the CODATA 2018 entry it claims (it does not, 5/5). A discover_papers run finding a post-2024 radius outside 0.83-0.88 fm would still not flip W10; it would move the pinned number.
